fields.mechanism: Electric power steering assist torque instability arises from dynamic coupling between road feedback and actuator control delays, causing transient loss of gain during low-temperature conditions.
fields.intervention: Implement a temperature-compensated adaptive gain controller in the EPS ECU that adjusts assist torque based on real-time fluid viscosity and motor temperature sensors at cold start.
fields.expected_effect: Restoration of consistent steering assist torque stability during cold start, eliminating intermittent assist loss.
fields.falsification_test: A/B test: Drive vehicle with EPS temperature-compensated control enabled vs. disabled in sub-freezing conditions; measure steering torque variance over 50 cold starts; if variance remains high in the disabled group and low in the enabled group, the mechanism is confirmed.

fields.intervention: Implement an advanced control algorithm that compensates for temperature-dependent motor resistance and sensor drift during cold start conditions to maintain stable assist torque output.
